name: Prepositions of time
note: Use at for clock times, night, the weekend and festivals (at 6, at night, at Christmas). Use on for days and dates (on Monday, on 5 June, on my birthday). Use in for months, years, seasons and parts of the day (in July, in 2020, in winter, in the morning).

questions.q: I was ______ a party last night.
We always eat a roast dinner ______ Christmas Day.
questions.fs: We always eat a roast dinner on Christmas Day.

questions.q: It often snows ______ January.
As a result of the very long heat wave last summer many of the rivers have now completely dried ______
questions.fs: As a result of the very long heat wave last summer many of the rivers have now completely dried up.

questions.q: I always get ______ early in the summer.
questions.fs: I always get up early in the summer.

questions.q: I'm now ready to turn ______ for the night but the worrying thing is I just can't remember what I had for supper.
questions.fs: I'm now ready to turn in for the night but the worrying thing is I just can't remember what I had for supper.

questions.q: I graduated from college ______ 2002.
questions.fs: I graduated from college in 2002.

questions.q: It was late April and the sun had disappeared behind dark heavy rain clouds but Andrew had already set ______ for the local pub.
questions.fs: It was late April and the sun had disappeared behind dark heavy rain clouds but Andrew had already set off for the local pub.

questions.q: Do you lock the front door ______ night?
questions.fs: Do you lock the front door at night?

questions.q: Teacher: Well if you started living in Paris in 1999 and you are still there, you say; I have been living there ______ 1999.
questions.fs: Teacher: Well if you started living in Paris in 1999 and you are still there, you say; I have been living there since 1999.

questions.q: Employee: It's Thursday of course. What do you want to know ______ ?
questions.fs: Employee: It's Thursday of course. What do you want to know for?

questions.q: You see I've just turned all the lights ______ ready for the night.
questions.fs: You see I've just turned all the lights out ready for the night.

questions.q: My brother is looking ______ his cat. It may be in the garden.
I'll meet you again ______ the weekend.
Shakespeare was born ______ 23 April 1564.
questions.fs: Shakespeare was born on 23 April 1564.

questions.q: George had a very well paid contract with a television advertiser of garden peas and he didn't want to fall out ______ the company.
questions.fs: George had a very well paid contract with a television advertiser of garden peas and he didn't want to fall out with the company.

questions.q: In Europe, autumn begins ______ September.
questions.fs: In Europe, autumn begins in September.

questions.q: She's ______ a high at the moment because everything is going her way.
questions.fs: She's on a high at the moment because everything is going her way.

questions.q: This summer we went ______ holiday to Greece.
questions.fs: This summer we went on holiday to Greece.

questions.q: The one day that many people love is Friday because that is when they can think about their time ______ at the weekend.
questions.fs: The one day that many people love is Friday because that is when they can think about their time off at the weekend.

questions.q: I like to go to bed ______ midnight on Saturdays.
questions.fs: I like to go to bed at midnight on Saturdays.

questions.q: He may be able to come to the party. ______ the other hand, he may be too busy.
The chairman of the board has been working in the finance industry ______ 1984.
questions.fs: The chairman of the board has been working in the finance industry since 1984.

questions.q: Old lady: Well you see this supermarket is so big I can't find the way ______ I've been here since Tuesday!
questions.fs: Old lady: Well you see this supermarket is so big I can't find the way out I've been here since Tuesday!

questions.q: That's what I would like ______ Christmas.
questions.fs: That's what I would like for Christmas.
